about: Examples for the point-of-view read (part 5 of docs/CLARITY-READ.md, tools/humanization/clarity_read.py make --kind pov). Joel, 2026-10-25 14:20 UTC, on the Inner Child guide: "make sure you use the new rule in the repo about marking wherever it looks like there's a lack of a real POV and just some generic portable prose/advice that should be replaced or cut" (the rule: project-sources/PRODUCTION-HUMANIZATION-PREFLIGHT.md, "Actual POV required", with its omission test first). The examples are what he did with such lines in the Inner Child guide: the cuts he took and why, the one passage he gave his own reason, and lines he kept, with his reasons, that a reader could have taken for portable advice. His words are quoted as he wrote them. Add his answers here as he gives them.

examples.label: POV (he replaced it with his reason)
examples.before: Some practitioners are gentle about it and walk you through the maze just fine. Others seem to leave people more split up than when they started. I wouldn't trust a model more just because there's a big institute behind it handing out certificates.
examples.what_he_did: A general critique with nobody's case behind it; three fresh readers called it "a summary of experience rather than a particular one". He replaced it with what a friend of his explained from her own healing, that knowing the parts can help but the growing map can overwhelm, so people already overwhelmed can come out more split up, and his own verdict: "I've seen many others echo this same evaluation, and it makes sense to me." (2026-10-25)

examples.label: CUT (he cut it)
examples.before: Yes, yes, it might feel a bit strange, seeing your own face from back then. But look at it gently and just notice what comes up.
examples.what_he_did: Cut, with the start of the next paragraph, which said to notice what comes up again: "this is the part that reads ai and it's actually redundant also" (2026-10-25).

examples.label: CUT (he cut it)
examples.before: You can always slow down and look closer when it helps.
examples.what_he_did: Cut, the nutshell's last line: "oh that was from GPT, i humanized it but didn't notice how jarring that last stupid sentence was" (2026-10-24).

examples.label: CUT (he cut it)
examples.section: Catch the Hook Before the Story Takes Over
examples.before: You can figure that out later.
examples.what_he_did: Cut: "it doesn't tell the reader the detective work can wait, that's what the prior sentence said.." (2026-10-24).

examples.label: CUT (he cut it)
examples.before: Or just nothing comes up, which is also completely OK.
examples.what_he_did: Cut ", which is also completely OK" (2026-10-24): "Or just nothing comes up" already makes it an ordinary outcome. His rewrites cut my tidy closers and quips the same way: "(this article included)", "I'd take that!", "If it still says no, that's your answer.", "(nobody's taking attendance)".

examples.label: POV (an "I'd" that was only an instruction)
examples.before: Before either one, I'd look for what exactly is in the way.
examples.what_he_did: He made it a plain instruction, "Before going with either of those paths, look for what exactly is in the way", and kept the "I'd" lines that are his own judgment: "I'd want to quit too", "I'd change course sooner". (2026-10-24)

examples.label: POV (he put in a story only he has)
examples.section: You Don't Need an Inner Monologue
examples.before: other people and things you have in your life
examples.what_he_did: He put his own moment in its place: "like that guy who found me in a random park crying one time, and asked me "What's wrong?"" (2026-10-24).

examples.label: KEEP (his point of view, though it looks like a disclaimer)
examples.before: I’m not pushing “toxic positivity.” Being thankful shouldn’t be pushed on people who just need to grieve for the moment.
examples.what_he_did: Kept: "it's an objection that so many people have raised to me" (2026-10-24). A line that answers what people actually say to him is his point of view.

examples.label: KEEP (his point of view, though it looks like a disclaimer)
examples.before: And I’m certainly not preaching “prosperity philosophy,” even though it can seem to start at that.
examples.what_he_did: Kept: "it's not just protecting the writer, it's naming a massive religious movement of fakery that i might get lumped into instnatly" (2026-10-24).

examples.label: KEEP (his point of view, though it looks like a hedge)
examples.what_he_did: Kept: "people often do fight too many battles that's why i say when feasible, like choose ur battles bro" (2026-10-24). And of "You don't have to pretend to believe anything, but": "it purposefully does take back because people may not just listen to my commands, they have their own ideas".
